pass_a_gloss: When Heracleon seemed to have observed most persuasively in these things that upon the former things “Believe me, woman” had not been said to her, but now this has been commanded to her, then he muddied his own word. For he says that the creation is a desert dwelling-place of beasts, which all before the law were worshiping; and Jerusalem the creator, whom the Jews were worshiping. You therefore, he says, will worship neither the creation nor the demiurge, but the Father of the truth. And he takes her along, he says, as already faithful and being numbered with the true worshipers. But if the angels do not worship the Father in Jerusalem, how will those better than those in Jerusalem not worship the Father?
pass_b_english: Heracleon thought he had spotted something clever: earlier Jesus had not said, [[“Believe me, woman,” >> Bible:John 4:21]] but now he commands it. That observation muddies his own case.

He says creation is a desert haunt of beasts, which all worshiped before the law; Jerusalem stands for the creator, whom the Jews worshiped. “You,” he says, “will worship neither creation nor the demiurge, but the Father of truth.” He even counts the woman already among the true worshipers.
But if angels do not worship the Father in Jerusalem, how can those greater than Jerusalem’s worshipers fail to worship the Father?
